chapter: Los Angeles: Chico Hamilton, Webster, Giuffre
title: Pacific Jazz, Dick Bock and Two Degrees East, Three Degrees West
summary: Recording for Dick Bock, including the record with John Lewis and Percy Heath.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: The other thing that was going on at that time was a lot of recording for Pacific Jazz label.
And you were on a lot of that.
Yeah. I think… I’m embarrassed. I can’t think of the guy’s name who

Dick Bock, that’s right. I was gonna say… yeah, Dick Bock, B-O-C-K, yeah. He was a good guy. And… Chico recorded for him. And then Dick put together this record that… it’s called Two Degrees East, Three Degrees West, which is, was an ironic title

because I was supposed to be one of the Three Degrees West. Bill Perkins played tenor and Chico played drums. And I was from Cleveland, so I wasn’t from the West Coast at all (laughs) and… and John Lewis was from Texas, I think, and Percy, he… Anyway, it was, it was great. It was Percy and John, and that’s where I kinda got to know John, who was an incredible help to me after that so…
